Functions and function maps

Most locomotives only need you to Load Function Map on the train form. Use this page when you want to browse the library, adapt a map for your own trains, or understand how functions work under the hood.

You can skip this at first. Add a train, load an existing map, and come back here if nothing quite matches — or if you want to tidy icons and order across several locos.

Function maps

A function map is a ready-made list of functions for a decoder or model (often matching a manufacturer’s numbering). Instead of wiring up F0, F1, F2 by hand for every locomotive, you load a map that already names and icons those slots.

Panels DCC includes a large — and continuously growing — library of function maps for off-the-shelf DCC-fitted models.

Open function maps on the Panels DCC website

Click a card to open that map and browse its functions. From there you can make a version for your own trains, or create a new map of your own.

Creating your own map

If you need a new map, start by finding an existing one that is as close as possible to what you want. That saves a lot of time.

You are looking for the list of functions — not necessarily in the right order. For example, many steam engines with sound share a similar set of sound functions, even when manufacturers arrange them differently. Manufacturers also have their own preferences for numbering and naming, so a map from the same brand is often a better starting point than one that merely looks similar.

When you build or edit a map, you pick each entry from the function library — the shared pool of named icons with on and off pictures. Prefer those existing functions and customise them where you can (there is a good generic lights icon, and general-purpose icons if you are stuck). You can add your own function, but that means creating pictures for both the on and off states, so it is usually better to reuse and adapt what is already there.

What is a function? A function is one decoder feature — lights, horn, coupling, a sound effect, and so on — shown as a named button with icons instead of a bare F number.

Each function has two pictures: one for off and one for on, so in Control you can see at a glance whether it is active.

Functions also have a behaviour type:

  • Latching — tap once to turn on, tap again to turn off. The feature stays in that state until you change it. Lights are usually latching: you turn them on for a while and leave them.
  • Momentary — the feature is only on while you hold the button; release and it stops. Horns and many sound effects are momentary — you would not want them stuck on after a tap.
Lights — latching (off / on)
Horn — momentary (off / on)

Getting latching vs momentary right matters. If a horn is set as latching by mistake, one tap leaves it sounding until you tap again. If lights are momentary, they only work while you hold the button.

In the map editor

Click Add New Function Map for a blank map, or open a close match and make a copy you can change. In the editor you can:

  • Add, remove, and drag rows to set which functions sit on which F numbers — and in which order.
  • Click an icon to open the picker. Search the library, then apply icon only or icon, name, and type.
  • Give the map a name and description so you can find it later.

Remember: the first six functions on a train are the ones shown beside the throttle in Control. Put the ones you use most at the top — you can do that on the map, or after you load the map onto a train.

Save when you are happy. You can then load that map onto any of your trains from the train form.

Add a custom function (optional)

Only needed when nothing in the library fits — even after searching for a generic icon.

Open functions on the Panels DCC website

Click Add New Function. Give it a name, choose latching or momentary, and supply icons for off and on. Your function then appears in the picker when you edit a map or a train.
